text:
maria: Heads-up — alert from prod: spikes in rpc latency and ~10% 5xxs from gpu-allocator in us-west-2. Initial traces point to DNS timeouts when resolving allocator-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local
liam: saw it too. errors are DNS timeout / SERVFAIL from the kube-dns path. metrics show coreDNS latency windowed around 150–600ms for a bunch of pods
arun: any recent changes to MTU or NIC offloads on the gpu hosts? we pushed a kernel/firmware roll last night to the 8-node gpu pool
maria: yep, the rolling kernel update landed around 03:30 UTC on that pool. telemetry bot shows increased retransmits east-west after that
cluster-telemetry-bot: noticed 12% increase in UDP reassembly errors on nic-ib0 in us-west-2-gpu between 03:25–04:10 UTC
erin: can someone paste coreDNS pod logs? I want to see if it's internal plugin failures or upstream 127.0.0.53 timeouts
maria: grabbing logs, short excerpt:
```
2026-03-18T03:31:12Z core-dns-0 kernel: IP: frag reassembly failed, packet dropped
2026-03-18T03:31:12Z coredns[1]: servfail for allocator-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local from 10.0.0.2:53
2026-03-18T03:31:13Z node-local-dns[abc]: restarting: timed out waiting for response
```
sam: that frag message screams MTU mismatch or offload bug. RDMA offload + UDP frag known to cause reassembly issues on some NIC firmware versions
liam: quick repro: on an affected gpu node: `dig +short @127.0.0.1 allocator-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local` hangs for 2s then nothing. `dig +short @10.0.0.10 allocator-service...` (coreDNS) returns fast
arun: interesting — node-local-dns to coreDNS path is fine, but node-local seems to be dropping packets before forwarding? could be iptables conntrack or eBPF sidecar?
maria: trying a local tcpdump (udp port 53) on node network interface, capturing a failing query. payload length ~1450 bytes, then a fragment, then nothing
erin: 1450 is dangerously close to 1500 MTU — if any encapsulation (vxlan/overhead) + offload weirdness will fragment. can we check mtu on host, on the pod veth, and any tunnel interfaces?
liam: `ip link show` on host: mtu 9000 (jumbo), vxlan0 mtu 1450 on our overlay (we set overlay-mtu=1450 in calico). kernel update might have changed offload handling so fragments are malformed
sam: workaround idea: disable UDP GRO/TSO/LRO for a suspect NIC (`ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`) on one node and retest dig. if that fixes, firmware/offload is culprit
arun: we should also try disabling node-local-dns on one node (set hostNetwork to true on a debug pod) to see if bypassing node-local cache alleviates the issue
maria: rolling repro plan: pick one affected node, disable offloads, tail tcpdump, run a synthetic load of 1000 DNS queries/s from a kube-proxy pod targeting node-local cache and coreDNS. capture success rate and p99 latency
erin: I'll coordinate a canary - pinging infra-ops to approve the transient change on 1/8 nodes. low blast radius
liam: also flagged potential GPU job impact — if allocator API gets 5xxs, pending job scheduling stalls and we start burning reserved GPUs. cost/compliance note: if this persists, we might need to shift some batch jobs to other region or preemptible pool to avoid paying for idle dedicated GPUs
maria: agreed. I'll add autoscaler rule to temporarily reduce new job acceptance if allocator errors exceed 5% for >5m
cluster-telemetry-bot: created incident ticket INF-2026-032: coreDNS-node-local-dns-frag-issues, assigned to eng-infra oncall
sam: once we validate offload bit, we should produce a host-firmware blocklist and roll FW or revert kernel change. if RDMA NICs are involved, coordinate with network team for vendor fix
erin: sounds good. next steps: 1) pick node and run `ethtool -k`/disable offloads 2) tcpdump capture 3) run synthetic dig load 4) swap node-local-dns pod to hostNetwork to test bypass 5) if repro -> roll AWS host-firmware rollback or disable offloads clusterwide temporarily
maria: I'll run step 1–4 now on node gpu-usw2-07 and report back in this thread. will also attach pcap and prometheus graphs when done :thumbsup:
